questions.prompt: Which statement about vacuum forming is correct?

choices.text: The vacuum sucks and pulls the soft plastic sheet down onto the mould
The sheet is formed while it is still cold and rigid
The vacuum removes the air beneath the pliable sheet, and unopposed outside air pressure pushes the sheet onto the mould.
The mould presses the sheet into shape by pushing down on it from above

questions.misconception: The vacuum sucks and pulls the soft plastic sheet down onto the mould.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: The vacuum sucks and pulls the soft plastic sheet down onto the mould. In fact The flat sheet is clamped in the frame and heated until pliable, the mould rises into the soft sheet, the vacuum then removes the air trapped beneath it, and the unopposed outside air pressure pushes the sheet onto every surface of the mould, where it cools, sets rigid, and is lifted off and trimmed.

questions.prompt: Why is the sheet heated before forming?

choices.text: To melt the sheet into a liquid that is poured over the mould
To make the thermoplastic pliable so it sags and can be pushed onto every surface of the mould
To make the sheet rigid so it holds its flat shape
To remove the air trapped beneath the sheet

questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: heating makes the clamped sheet pliable and sagging, ready for outside air pressure to form it onto the mould.

questions.prompt: A student says the vacuum pulls the soft sheet onto the mould. Explain, in two sentences, what actually forms the sheet.
questions.answer: The flat sheet is clamped in the frame and heated until pliable, the mould rises into the soft sheet, the vacuum then removes the air trapped beneath it, and the unopposed outside air pressure pushes the sheet onto every surface of the mould, where it cools, sets rigid, and is lifted off and trimmed.
questions.explanation: The deciding habit is to separate the two jobs: the vacuum only removes air, and unopposed outside air pressure does the pushing.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state what happens after the sheet has been formed onto the mould, and why that step matters.
questions.answer: The formed sheet cools on the mould and sets rigid, so the shell keeps the mould shape when it is lifted off and trimmed.
questions.explanation: Scene 4 shows cooling and release: cooling sets the plastic rigid before the shell is lifted off and trimmed.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the vacuum-forming stages in order?

choices.text: Clamp the sheet, heat until pliable, remove the air so pressure forms it, cool rigid and trim
Heat until pliable, clamp the sheet, cool rigid, remove the air so pressure forms it
Remove the air, clamp the sheet, trim the shell, heat until pliable
Cool rigid, heat until pliable, clamp the sheet, remove the air

questions.explanation: Scene 1 clamps, scene 2 heats, scene 3 forms by removing air so pressure pushes, and scene 4 cools, releases and trims.
